label: sealed-holdout-pilot
caseOrder: lexicographic ID, integration supplemental after main cases
budgetDisclosure: 60 × 6 × (100000 + 8192) = 38,949,120 local admission projection exceeds shared quota; serial admission stops when insufficient. Wire has no output ceiling, so quota is not a hard billed-spend cap. Reasoning is a component of output, not added twice. Monetary tariffs unknown.

evaluationSeed.meaning: Execution seed for the isolated evaluator, not an LLM sampling parameter

targetStatus: Proposed pilot point targets from specs/10-validation.md; reported with n and Wilson 95% intervals. Not formally approved by the spending authorization. Zero unsafe autoapply and zero critical false repair are noncompensatory.
authorization: Operator-authorized (2026-10-09) paid model rounds for this evaluation, and re-authorized explicitly on 2026-10-12 ("autorizado") to re-measure healing after the VAL-016 prompt-leak invalidation of rounds 6-8. Single serialized round on the sealed reference-hostel holdout after deterministic controls and policy probes pass. No replacement cases, model retries outside the gateway, manual approvals during the round, or reruns of this registration; the round starts once. The reference-hostel family was authored after the implementation freeze d484cf2 (leakage-guarded harness with opaque plan names; the same product implementation as round 8 b5cd410 plus the harness guard) and sealed before the first evaluated call. Provider traffic is routed through the local leakage guard, which blocks and invalidates the round on any sealed label, mutant, case ID, oracle name or author prose in a request. Targets are unchanged from round 8.
healingReviewPolicy: Safe abstention: no manual approval is collected during the round. A candidate without semantic-equivalence proof stays proposed/manual-only and scores no automatic-healing success; all 12 drift cases stay in the primary denominator.
stopPolicy: two consecutive terminal provider transport failures
sealed-label leakage detected by the prompt guard
labelReview: validation: automated-only (ADR-012). Labels are declared and sealed (SHA-256) before the first evaluated call; no human review is performed or simulated. Cases declared disputed before sealing form a separate stratum.
limitations: The holdout family was never used in development; the evaluated implementation is frozen at the declared commit and the family was authored after that freeze and sealed before the first evaluated call. Authorship timestamps and development use are declared, not proven.
Cases within one application family are correlated; corpus-derived denominators do not establish independent families or graduation, and there is no <1% rare-event claim.
Remote model snapshot unavailable; monetary tariffs unknown.
Authored fixture plans are not model-generated main-case plans; no integration workflow case (supplemental) is included in this holdout, and driver-bound upload fixtures are not exercised.
Wilson lower bound at n=12 is about 0.758 even for 12/12, so a lower bound >=0.8 is not a reachable pilot gate; point targets are reported with n and intervals.
Source-grounded fix targets are exercised by deterministic controls; live cases receive no synthetic source catalogs.

The registered 7200000 ms wall-time ceiling (checker-fixed) may truncate the round with stop reason wall_time_exhausted, because calibration calls took up to about 300 s at xhigh. A truncated round is reported as partial, never as a complete measurement, and unrun cases count as misses only in the disclosed partial denominators.

One synthetic reference-hostel family authored by the implementing team (an agent) after the implementation freeze d484cf2 and sealed before the first evaluated call; automated-only validation under ADR-012 makes no claim of independent review or of generalization beyond the sealed family. Authorship timestamps and development use are declared, not proven.

ho-drift-10, ho-drift-11 and ho-drift-12 are manual-only by design (changed accessible name, child-combinator CSS path, detached-to-hidden wait); the deterministic policy probes must confirm ho-drift-01 to 09 are policy-applied and 10 to 12 stay proposed. They stay in the safe-healing denominator, so 9/12 is the structural ceiling of safe automatic healing for this corpus.

This round exists because rounds 6-8 sent the sealed case ID inside plan.name to the healing model (VAL-016). The harness now anonymizes plan names and routes the provider through a leakage guard; the guard checks requests, not model behavior, and a clean guard does not prove the model had no other source of the labels.

The registered 7200000 ms wall-time ceiling (checker-fixed) may truncate the round with stop reason wall_time_exhausted, because calibration calls took up to about 300 s at xhigh. A truncated round is reported as partial, never as a complete measurement.

preFreezeControlsContract.output: Exclusive OUT_DIR/manifest.json plus all 30 per-case evidence JSON files; manifest hashes each retained case evidence
preFreezeControlsContract.freezeCommand: node tools/dist/evals/m3.js freeze REGISTRATION CONTROLS_DIR/manifest.json POLICY_PROBES_DIR/manifest.json
preFreezeControlsContract.evidence: Actual model-free Docker run/revision IDs, exact expected failing steps, outcome/gate/reason codes, image IDs, bound plan hashes, independent SQLite/raw-HTTP oracle observations, authored drift-candidate pass and semantic assertion failure. Guard has one deliberate positive request then zero execution model requests. Unsatisfied cases are blocked; boolean-only manifests refused.
preFreezeControlsContract.policyProbes: Deterministic local-provider acceptance: authored candidates for all 12 drift cases pass through the real HealingService under the frozen implementation manifest; records policy eligibility or manual-only reasons. Not model quality.

predecessor.decision: Rounds 6-8 healing-stage evidence is void under VAL-016 (plan.name carried the sealed case ID into the healing prompt); round 8 diagnosis figures stand. Round 9 re-measures healing and diagnosis on a new sealed family with the leakage guard.
